subject.title: [Feature]: Add provider-profile routing policies for multi-account OAuth/API pools (starting with google-gemini-cli)

question: Should OpenClaw core add a first-class opt-in provider-profile pool routing API, or should the remaining needs be handled through narrower auth.cooldowns/profile-rotation fixes and provider/plugin-specific surfaces?
rationale: The requested behavior defines new config schema, routing semantics, session stickiness modes, concurrency/accounting state, and observability across auth-provider and session-state boundaries, which automation cannot choose safely.

options.title: Keep Canonical Core Design
options.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical design tracker and require a maintainer-approved opt-in core API before implementation.

options.title: Narrow To Existing Repairs
options.body: Close or split the broad pool API direction and track only concrete fixes such as same-provider rotation, bucket cooldowns, and UI exposure in narrower issues.

options.title: Route To Provider Plugins
options.body: Require provider-specific plugins or sidecars to own pool behavior unless they first identify a missing core extension API.

recommendation.title: Keep Canonical Core Design
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical design tracker and require a maintainer-approved opt-in core API before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant history points to steipete for sticky auth-profile rotation, usage headers, provider auth aliases, and configurable failover semantics.
